objective: Manage the identity life cycle: define roles, provision, review and deprovision access
secondaryObjectives: Recognize access risks: privilege creep, orphaned accounts, and shared and service accounts
Apply the principle of least privilege and separation of duties to an access request

sources.cite: ISC2, CC Certification Exam Outline (effective 2026-09-01), Domain 3: Identity And Access Management (IAM) Concepts

sources.cite: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (release 5.2.0), AC-2 Account Management and AC-2(3) Disable Accounts

brief.situation: You are a junior security analyst at Larchmont Supply, a fictional distributor. At 08:30 on Monday the queue shows a VPN sign-in and heavy file-share reading by j.okafor, a contractor on the ERP integration project. You are not sure yet whether j.okafor still works here. The quarterly access review is also due today. Work the queue, contain what needs containing, and write it up.
handover: You can disable accounts and revoke sessions under the account-management procedure; the incident handler on call owns any declared incident.
Accounts are disabled first and removed only after the retention period; logs are kept for investigations.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. Whoever is using the account keeps working on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you close the incident you notify, record it and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the incident record: what this was, how you closed it, and what in the identity life cycle failed.

parts.label: Recognition
parts.criteria: Identifies an orphaned account of a leaver still in use, confirmed against HR before acting on it, not a routine sign-in or a phished employee.
parts.modelAnswer: HR shows the contract ended Friday and the termination ticket was never worked, so an account that should not exist was being used from outside.

parts.label: Containment
parts.criteria: Disables the account and revokes its sessions (a password change or an address block alone leaves access), looks for anything the account created, keeps the logs, and does not delete the account before the evidence and retention needs are met.
parts.modelAnswer: I disabled the account and revoked its VPN and SSO sessions together, searched for keys it had made, and exported the logs; deletion waits for the retention period.

parts.label: Life cycle
parts.criteria: Names deprovisioning as the failed step and fixes the process; treats the mover's leftover rights and the shared account as access-review items, after the live intrusion.
parts.modelAnswer: Deprovisioning failed because the leaver ticket was not acted on; the leaver process now opens an access-removal task. The mover's Sales rights are privilege creep and the shared account goes to named accounts in the review.

expertPath.text: Check HR: the contract ended Friday and the termination ticket is open. Review the sessions: VPN and SSO from outside.
Disable the account and revoke its sessions together; search for keys or accounts it created.
Export the logs, tell the incident handler, close the termination ticket and fix the leaver step.
Access review: remove the mover's Sales rights with her manager; plan named accounts for warehouse-shared.

contained.headline: Good: deprovisioned, fixed at the cause
contained.body: An orphaned account is a life-cycle failure, not a login problem. You confirmed, cut every path, kept the evidence and fixed the leaver step.

containedLate.headline: Contained, with gaps
containedLate.body: The account is closed. The criteria show what cost you: data out first, a late key search, late logs, or no process fix.

dataGone.headline: The files left first
dataGone.body: Blocking an address or resetting a password leaves a valid account working. Disable and revoke together, early.

evidenceLost.headline: Evidence deleted
evidenceLost.body: Disable first, export the logs, and delete only when retention allows. Deleting destroyed the record of what was taken.

leftOpen.headline: A way in was left open
leftOpen.body: An account that can still sign in, or a key it made, keeps the door open after the case is closed.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No incident record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: A sign-in by someone whose contract ended is an orphaned account in use: deprovisioning failed. Confirm with HR, then disable the account and revoke its sessions together (a password reset or an address block leaves access), search for keys or accounts it created, export the logs, and keep the account disabled for retention rather than deleting it. Tell the incident handler, close the termination ticket and fix the leaver step. The mover's leftover rights and the shared account are review items, worked after the live intrusion.
